title: Degradation Communications: Tactical Dossier for Sales & Ops
content:
TL;DR
This dossier provides short, tactical messaging and scenario playcards for sales, customer success, and on-call ops to explain Redwood’s graceful degradation guarantees and fallback choreography. Focus: clear trust signals, specific fallback behaviors, competitive differentiators, and suggested verbatim scripts for customer conversations across enterprise and developer audiences.

Audience and use cases
- Sales (enterprise pre-sales, AE conversations): reassure prospects on continuity and predictable behavior under load or region outages.
- Customer Success / Support: post-incident explanations and SLA/commitment framing.
- Solutions / Partners: technical trade-offs, integration guidance for multi-region routing and model variants.
- Marketing / Product: short copy suggestions for website and datasheets.

Core positioning statements (one-liners)
- For engineering teams who need inference that keeps working even when systems strain, Redwood offers predictable fallbacks and transparent degradation so customer apps don’t fail silently.
- We surface exactly what changed (latency vs. model quality) and why — reducing surprise, restoring trust, and enabling measurable recovery.

Key buyer concerns we must answer
- "Will my app return errors or degraded content when capacity is constrained?" -> Answer: Redwood never drops requests silently; requests are routed to fallback model variants or a dedicated reserve pool based on your policy.
- "How will users notice degradation?" -> Answer: Degradation is graded and communicated (latency-first, quality-second) with explicit headers/traces for observability.
- "How do you compare to cloud-hosted model endpoints or do-it-yourself infra?" -> Answer: We provide out-of-the-box routing, KV/prefix caching, and multi-region failover tuned for inference economics — vs. DIY, you avoid brittle orchestration and costly overprovisioning.

Graded degradation model (shorthand)
- Tier 0: Healthy — requested model runs on primary region and primary variant.
- Tier 1: Latency elevation — longer tails, but model and quality unchanged. System signals tail latency and can optionally route to a lower-latency replica.
- Tier 2: Economical fallback — system routes to a quantized / smaller variant with documented quality delta (we show sample prompt regressions).
- Tier 3: Capacity isolation — dedicated reserved pool engaged (for customers with commits).
- Tier 4: Partial feature disable — non-essential routes (e.g., long-context summarization) are rate-limited while core inference continues.

Fallback choreography (customer-facing phrasing + equivalent technical behavior)
- Phrase: "If traffic exceeds capacity, we transparently route to a highly-compatible model variant so your product stays online; you can see the switch in logs and compare outputs."
  Technical: automated routing policy => compatible model family (same tokenizer, smaller hidden dims), trace header: X-RW-Fallback: quantized-v2, quality-score tag.
- Phrase: "We prioritize correctness for critical requests and latency for interactive flows. You set the rules — we execute them."
  Technical: per-route policy: critical=true => route to dedicated pool or increase priority; interactive routes => lower-batch timeout and fallback to low-latency replicas.

Example scripts (short)
- Sales elevator (30s): "We help you avoid the hard choice between overprovisioning and user-visible failures. Redwood uses staged fallbacks and per-route policies so you maintain uptime and diagnose exactly what changed — latency, model variant, or rate-limiting — without guessing."
- CS proactive email after incident (subject: Short service impact, what changed): "We observed regional degradation yesterday. Your traffic was routed to a validated quantized fallback for 17 minutes to preserve availability. We’ve attached sample outputs and latency/usage graphs; no customer data left the configured region."
- Support quick reply (chat): "Short answer: your requests were served by our fallback model for ~10min due to a regional capacity spike. We log the variant used and you can compare outputs in the Trace view; we also opened a ticket to review policy thresholds with your team."

Competitive notes (how to frame differences)
- Against large cloud provider managed endpoints: emphasize our model-variant awareness, built-in quality regression metrics, and cheaper fallbacks (quantization profiles tuned for each model) — they offer endpoints but rarely provide verified quality deltas for fallback variants.
- Against self-hosted inference runtimes: emphasize product velocity + operational safety: same API across hosted/dedicated/private with rollout and observability primitives; customers avoid building multi-region routing and rollback logic.
- Against focused LLM-API startups: call out predictable economics at scale (batching + KV cache) and multi-tiered SLAs (reserved pools + automated fallbacks).

Risk framing and mitigation suggestions for sales/CS
- Risk: customer worries about silent quality loss.
  Mitigation: show side-by-side examples (gold vs. fallback) in onboarding, provide default threshold settings to disable fallbacks for critical routes.
- Risk: compliance/regional data residency concerns during multi-region failover.
  Mitigation: advertise explicit region pinning: policy prevents cross-region fallback unless customer allows it; audit logs show every decision.
- Risk: perceived complexity of policies.
  Mitigation: provide three canned policy templates (conservative, balanced, permissive) and a one-click suggestion engine in Optimize.

Suggested assets to include in next enablement pack
- Playcard PDF for AEs: 1-page flowchart + two example scripts + competitive bullets.
- Sample trace snippets and JSON logs showing fallback headers.
- Two-page explainer on "quantized fallbacks" with measured quality deltas on common prompts.

Incident narrative templates (for various audiences)
- External: short, focus on impact and customer-facing action. Example: "We experienced degraded performance in eu-west-1 between 02:14–02:31 UTC. For affected traffic we used an approved, validated fallback model to maintain availability; latency and quality metrics are attached. We’ve completed a post-incident review and are implementing a region capacity buffer."
- Partner / Security ops: include PSIRT-style details: what changed, whether PII left region, mitigation steps, relevant tickets/PRs.
- Engineering postmortem intro for public/partner consumption: succinct timeline, root cause hypothesis, immediate mitigations, next steps (policy tuning, reserve capacity commit for customers >X QPS).

Measurement and trust signals to surface in UI and scripts
- Trace header and human-readable tag explaining fallback reason (e.g. capacity_spike, region_failover, policy_forcing).
- Side-by-side outputs (primary vs. fallback) with a simple quality metric and examples.
- Estimated economic delta (cost/token) when fallback engaged — helps billing conversations.

Open questions / decisions for product and GTM
- Default policy: Should new customers have conservative (no cross-region fallbacks) or balanced (allow same-cloud-region failover)? Recommendation: balanced with clear opt-out for strict residency needs.
- Fallback transparency level: default to show fallback headers + provide an opt-in detailed trace export.
- Customer-facing SLA language: draft a short appendix that maps degraded tiers to customer commitments (e.g., availability target met with fallback engaged vs. without).

Notes to self / next steps
- Build quick A/B pack for AE enablement with three customer personas: startup-reactive, platform-team-risk-averse, regulated-enterprise.
- Coordinate with Applied ML to generate model-fallback sample sets for top 5 open models in catalog (action: Carlos).
- Add a checkbox in the Console rollout UI: "Show fallback trace headers to users" and document implications (Marta/Evan).

Appendix: short technical mapping (non-nested bullet list)
- KV/prefix cache: reduces load during surges, prevents repeated re-computation for conversational contexts.
- Quantized fallback: smaller model binaries, 4-bit/8-bit profiles, validated on prompt suites to produce expected deltas.
- Multi-region routing: health-check-driven, policy-guarded; supports region pinning.
- Dedicated pool: reserved GPU capacity with SLA that bypasses shared fallbacks.
- Rollout policies: canary, blue-green, automatic rollback on quality regressions.

End of dossier — use this as the working source for the one-page playcard and the AE enablement slide.

(Informal notes: keep language concrete, avoid marketing-speak; customers respond better to "what changed, where, and how we fixed it".)
